response: The EU’s GDPR, effective since May 2018, imposes strict data-protection rules on any organization processing EU residents’ data, including rights to access, erasure, and explicit consent, breach notification within 72 hours, and fines of up to 4% of global annual revenue or €20 million. Major penalties have hit tech giants—Meta was fined €1.2 billion in 2023, Amazon €746 million, and Google over €200 million—and the regulation inspired similar laws like California’s CCPA and Brazil’s LGPD. Critics cite compliance burdens on small businesses, user frustration with cookie banners, and uneven enforcement, but GDPR has nonetheless enshrined data privacy as a fundamental right and set the global standard for data protection.
